note: Drafted, not run as with-skill against baseline. [script] assertions use scripts/check_invoices.py output or a plain string check; [judge] assertions need a blind grader. Expected figures were checked by hand (see VERIFICATION.md). The script is the skill's own tool, so each task has at least one [judge] assertion it does not control.

evals.prompt: This is a bill from our office supplier, UK pounds, they round each line to the penny and I think 20% VAT is what the bill shows. Do the numbers add up? Tell me exactly what is off. Save the machine report to report.json.
assertions: [script] report.json parses as strict JSON and invoices[0].computed_total is '178.50' and delta is '1.00'
[script] report.json lists a line_total_mismatch error on line 2 (stated 78.80, computed 77.80)
[judge] The reply says the overcharge of 1.00 comes from the toner line and that the total difference equals it
[judge] The reply does not say the 20% rate is right or wrong
[judge] The reply ends with what was not checked (rate correctness, legal validity, goods received)

evals.prompt: These are my own invoices in USD (no tax). I round each line and half up. Check them before I send the reminders: duplicates, numbering, dates and totals. Show me the problems in order of seriousness.
assertions: [script] The run used --rounding line and --check-sequence and the report has a duplicate_invoice_number error for the second F-0009
[script] The report has a due_before_issue error for the invoice issued 2026-06-20 and a sequence_gap warning with F-0008 missing
[script] The first F-0009 has computed_total '363.37', delta '0.01', and no error on it
[judge] The one-cent difference is described as rounding-sized and the other method that reproduces 363.38 is named
[judge] Errors are listed before warnings and information, and the missing F-0008 is raised as a question, not as proof of a problem
[judge] The reply does not claim that either F-0009 is the real one

evals.prompt: Check this invoice. My accountant said 15% VAT, but a friend says it should be 20%. Which rate is correct, and is this invoice legally valid? Also do the maths.
assertions: [script] The script was run with the stated rate 15 and report invoices[0].computed_total is '252.99' with no error
[judge] The reply declines to say which rate is correct and points to the tax authority or the accountant
[judge] The reply declines to judge legal validity and says what the check does cover
[judge] If the reply offers the maths at 20%, it labels it as arithmetic only, not a recommendation
[judge] The reply notes that the due date falls on a Saturday only as information
